Use the [lesson](../04-proportions-and-sample-size.qmd) for the checked case introductions and source limits. Submit a short Quarto report with calculations, units, assumptions, and interpretation.

1. Reproduce the 95% tee-time Wald interval and interpret its margin in percentage points.
2. Calculate a 90% interval from the same counts. Compare widths without treating them as different datasets.
3. Reproduce both 95% planning sample sizes for E=.025. Then halve E and compare the unrounded required sizes.
4. Explain why ceiling(), not round(), is required and why p*=.50 is conservative in this formula.
5. For Lloyd's original planning extension, find n for a \$1 margin at 95% confidence. State the role and units of the planning SD.
6. Explain why default prop.test() may give different limits from the lesson and why large n alone cannot fix nonresponse bias.
